judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback lookup was rewritten to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which searches for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId even in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy/undefined, so it always yields undefined. When updateEvent is called without externalCalendarId (e.g. reschedule flows that rely on destinationCalendar), calendarId becomes undefined instead of the previously-used destinationCalendar.externalId, so the update targets a wrong/undefined calendar and the event update fails or hits the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` fallback was changed to:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the branch where the fallback should use `destinationCalendar`), the `.find()` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to `undefined`, which will almost always fail and return `undefined`. This breaks the intended behavior of using the event’s destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` is provided, potentially causing updates to target the wrong calendar (e.g., default/primary) or fail due to an undefined calendarId.
